reexecuted_commands.observed: Go has 'func (w WaitStatus) Stopped() bool { return w&mask == stopped && Signal(w>>shift) != SIGSTOP }', where SIGSTOP = 0x11 on darwin. Darwin defines WIFSTOPPED(x) as (_WSTATUS(x) == _WSTOPPED && WSTOPSIG(x) != 0x13), where 0x13 is SIGCONT. Go therefore classifies a SIGSTOP stop as Continued() on darwin.

refuted_claims.claim: REPORT.md (round 3b, line 361): 'SIGSTOP and SIGTTOU stops are mirrored as SIGTSTP'. Round 3c (lines 435-436) says the darwin SIGSTOP variant is only that 'the shell did not report the job stopped within 4 s'.
refuted_claims.evidence: This is false on darwin. A SIGSTOP stop of the child is never seen as a stop. Go's syscall_bsd.go WaitStatus.Stopped() excludes SIGSTOP (0x11), but darwin's WIFSTOPPED excludes 0x13 (SIGCONT), so the Wait4 loop in internal/run/run_unix.go falls through and heimdall-proto exits 255. The child is abandoned stopped in an orphaned group and gets SIGHUP+SIGCONT, then EIO. The meta file records CHILD_EXITED with exit_code -1. Observed for both self-stop and an external kill -STOP, on bash and zsh, for both r3b and r3c (detail/detail-darwin-1.txt, detail/detail-darwin-ext.txt). The harness observation agrees: child and parent are null (gone). The fix round disclosed it did not investigate this, so the characterization is incomplete rather than a hidden regression.

defects.description: darwin only, pre-existing (identical on round 3b), not introduced by round 3c. When the run child is stopped by SIGSTOP in exclusive mode, whether it stops itself or someone runs kill -STOP <child>, heimdall-proto exits 255 at once. It does not mirror the stop. The child is left stopped in an orphaned process group, so it gets SIGHUP+SIGCONT and then EIO on terminal reads. --meta-file records CHILD_EXITED with exit_code -1 and signal null. Root cause: Go's syscall_bsd.go WaitStatus.Stopped() excludes SIGSTOP (0x11), but darwin's WIFSTOPPED excludes 0x13 (SIGCONT). ws.Stopped() is false, the loop breaks, and ExitStatus() returns -1. Remedy for the prototype or production: decode the raw status (w&0x7f==0x7f gives stopped, with signal w>>8) instead of trusting ws.Stopped() on darwin. Escalation: whether §4 'does not exit first' / no orphaned child and the meta exit_code semantics gate this case beyond the §9.4 SIGSTOP self-stop recorded item is a contract question.

REPORT.md is inaccurate about the defect above. Line 361 says SIGSTOP stops are mirrored as SIGTSTP; on darwin they never reach mirrorStop. Lines 435-436 describe the darwin SIGSTOP variant only as 'shell did not report the job stopped within 4 s', leaving out that heimdall-proto exits 255 and abandons the child.

summary:
I found no fault in the round-3c change, and the harness verdict holds when re-run independently. The change is a narrow signal.Notify(SIGPIPE) that applies to every subcommand except run and tui.

My /tmp rebuild reproduces all four digests in dist/manifest.json. Harness 2.4.2 on my build passed 139/139 on darwin-arm64 (exit 0) and 139/139 on linux-arm64 via run.sh (exit 0).

K12 closed-stdout parity holds on both OSes for every subcommand, success and error results alike. This includes cases the harness does not cover: stderr closed, both streams closed, fd 1 closed, SIGPIPE inherited as ignored, and a reader that closes mid-output (Linux only). Round 3b differs in 26 of 114 case/setup pairs; round 3c in 0. The new Go test and the selftest check go red on round 3b and green on round 3c.

I compared round 3b and 3c builds in 112 pty scenarios under bash and zsh on both OSes. They covered:
- child self-stop with TSTP, STOP, TTIN and TTOU, repeated three times like ssh ~^Z
- Ctrl-Z, fg and bg
- explicit signals in shared and exclusive layouts, nohup, pipelines and sh -c
- EPIPE
- hangup

The comparison shows no regression: 0 differing fields on darwin, and on Linux 3 duplicate-count variances that K6b allows, with no signal lost.

Two of my early probe runs were invalid. One had a reentrancy bug in the probe child, and in the other the probe was started from a background subshell. I re-ran both and kept and labelled them.

Independently of round 3c, I found a pre-existing, non-gated darwin defect that REPORT.md misdescribes. A SIGSTOP stop of the run child, self-sent or external, makes heimdall-proto exit 255 and abandon the child. The child is orphaned and HUP'd, and the meta file records exit_code -1. The cause is Go's BSD WaitStatus.Stopped() treating SIGSTOP as "continued" on darwin. I am escalating whether §4 gates this.
